-73.98030,40.78530.name: Metropolitan Reproductive Medicine, PC
-73.98030,40.78530.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Susan Lobel, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

10.25745,53.66307.name: Klinik Manhagen
10.25745,53.66307.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. Operated by Klinik Manhagen GmbH & Co. KG. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

139.69875,35.66154.name: Hamamatsu Pharma Research, Inc. 1-3-7, Shinmiyakoda, Hamana-ku HAMAMATSU, SHIZUOKA, JAPAN Tel: +81-53-543-4543 Fax: +81-53-543-6444
139.69875,35.66154.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of CMIC. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-79.37847,43.65853.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, September 2025
-79.37847,43.65853.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, September 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-51.52012,-29.16567.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.embrios.com.br. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

-46.73183,-23.56750.name: Laboratório de Virologia Clínica e Molecular do Instituto de Ciências Biomédicas (ICB-II)
-46.73183,-23.56750.state: Av. Prof. Lineu Prestes, nº 2415 Butantã - São Paulo/SP - CEP 05508-00, Brazil
-46.73183,-23.56750.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Universidade de São Paulo. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on human health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

103.79000,1.30000.name: Lonza Singapore / biologics cluster
103.79000,1.30000.desc: Part of Singapore's deliberate build-out of biologics manufacturing, alongside the tax and land policy that brought it there. A state can acquire an industry this way in a decade, and the resulting capacity means therapies approved elsewhere are physically made in a country with no say in whether they were approved.

44.77700,41.72300.name: Eliava Institute
44.77700,41.72300.desc: Has treated patients with phages continuously in Tbilisi since 1923, through the period when the rest of the world abandoned the approach for antibiotics. Its collection and its clinical records are the longest-running body of experience anywhere, and they sit outside the regulatory framework every other country now applies.

6.13900,46.23200.name: UN Secretary-General's Mechanism for investigation of alleged use
6.13900,46.23200.state: Geneva — UN Office for Disarmament Affairs
6.13900,46.23200.desc: The only standing international capability to investigate an alleged use of biological weapons, since the Biological Weapons Convention has no verification system of its own. It relies on a roster of experts and laboratories nominated by member states and can only be triggered by the Secretary-General — an investigative body with no inspectors of its own.

-77.01100,38.89300.name: Federal Register — biotechnology notices and comment periods
-77.01100,38.89300.state: Washington DC — 800 North Capitol Street NW
-77.01100,38.89300.desc: Where US petitions for deregulation, permit notices and environmental assessments are announced, with a comment period usually of thirty to sixty days. Comments filed inside it are part of the record and the agency must address them; comments after it are correspondence. It offers email alerts filtered by subject, which is the practical answer to the fact that thirty days is short if you hear on day twenty-eight.
